either is non-zero. A batch whose custom ids no longer match its

entry.title: Key a judge verdict by subject and artifact; keep legacy verdicts on …
entry.content:
Key a judge verdict by subject and artifact; keep legacy verdicts on their own key

JudgeKey gains a subject part (judge:RUBRIC_SHA:SUBJECT:IDENTITY:ROLE);
for_question and for_rule set it from the question's subject and the
rule's note id, so a judged Rule and the judge backend still meet on
one row. A fit verdict cached for one word no longer answers another
word's question. Migrated legacy verdicts keep the old shape through
LegacyVerdictKey, and a migrate re-run still finds them. submit refuses
two prepared questions sharing one key (spec 3 r12 §4, spec 2 r8 §4).

entry.title: Judge a need's unjudged candidates before asking any source
entry.content:
Judge a need's unjudged candidates before asking any source

attempts.assess_first(ctx, need) asks the fit questions on the need's
candidates with no verdict under the current rubric and nothing else:
no source ask, no outcome row. None when none awaits or every awaiting
question was excluded; the run loop then falls through to the source.
Assess-first runs before source selection, the budget check and the
exhausted check (spec 3 r11 §5, §7).

entry.title: Fold the candidates awaiting a current verdict; make that the queue's…
entry.content:
Fold the candidates awaiting a current verdict; make that the queue's rubric lever

unjudged_candidates(cache, subject, kind, current_rubric) names a need's
candidate shas with no judge verdict under the current rubric for its
role. The queue's bucket-2 rubric lever is that fold: a stale verdict on
a sha that is not a candidate is no lever. An exhausted need with such a
candidate stays queued (spec 3 r11 §6).

entry.content:
Revise spec 2 to r7 and spec 3 to r11: assess-first

is judged before any source is asked; no source ask, no outcome row.
§6: the queue's rubric lever is that same fold, and an exhausted need
with such a candidate stays queued. §7 and §10 follow.

Spec 2 §4: the deck's current picture migrates as a candidate, one
provide row per joined word (backend legacy-current), no outcome row.

the migrated picture sat unjudged; a stale legacy verdict on a

entry.title: Strip judge answer fences; refuse a drafter answer with no drafts
entry.content:
Strip judge answer fences; refuse a drafter answer with no drafts

The fit, sentence and preference parsers accept a fenced JSON body
through the helper the drafter already used. LlmBackend appends only
a completion its producer recognizes; the sentence drafter recognizes
a body with drafts. A Forvo re-lookup that fails after an item stored
is a transient fetch. Stale prose on transient outcomes, the batch
status values, and the duration backend's contract corrected; a
negative test for judge.max_tokens.

Evidence: whole-branch review 2026-09-07.

entry.title: Configure judge.max_tokens; adaptive thinking needs at least 16000
entry.content:
Configure judge.max_tokens; adaptive thinking needs at least 16000

Both paid transports send judge.max_tokens (4096 by default). The
loader refuses thinking: adaptive below 16000.

Evidence: the first cutover run's 4096 tokens went entirely to thinking.

entry.title: Name the curated and tokenizer version in the fills key
entry.content:
Name the curated and tokenizer version in the fills key

A fills verdict depends on words.yaml, targets.yaml and the tokenizer;
its key carries a sha of the two files and the tokenizer's name and
version, so an edit to any of them is a new ask.

entry.title: Exclude a recording the duration check cannot read
entry.content:
Exclude a recording the duration check cannot read

A missing artifact, or one ffprobe rejects, is a PreparationError:
excluded for the run, never cached, never unreachable. Only an ffprobe
that cannot run is a transport error.
